content:
Rational numbers are where Class 7 maths grows up: suddenly numbers have signs AND fraction bars at the same time. One misplaced minus and a whole question collapses. The free IMO Class 7 Rational Numbers online test below has 10 exam-pattern MCQs with instant scoring. Treat it as a diagnostic. Every explanation tells you what to revise.

What the IMO asks from Rational Numbers in Class 7

  • Standard form (positive denominator, lowest terms).
  • Comparing and ordering with negatives, e.g. −2/5 vs −5/6.
  • All four operations on rational numbers.
  • Rational numbers between two given numbers.
  • Representing p/q on the number line.

Key facts and formulas to revise first

  • 48/−60 in standard form is −4/5 — the minus always moves up.
  • Between any two rational numbers there are infinitely many more — average them to find one.
  • −2/5 = −0.4 beats −5/6 ≈ −0.833 — with negatives, closer to zero is BIGGER.
  • q can never be 0 in p/q: division by zero is undefined.

Mistakes that cost Olympiad marks

  • Ranking negatives by digit size instead of number-line position.
  • Leaving answers with a negative denominator.
  • Assuming there is a "next" rational number after a given one.

questions.q: A rational number is written as p/q where p and q are integers. Which of the following can q never be?
questions.explanation: A rational number p/q requires q ≠ 0, because division by zero is undefined. So q can never be 0.

questions.q: What is the sum of 3/5 and −2/7?

questions.explanation: The order of the two addends is swapped without changing the sum. That is the commutative property of addition.

questions.q: What is the additive inverse of −7/12?
questions.explanation: The additive inverse of x is −x: the number that adds to it to give 0. −7/12 + 7/12 = 0, so the answer is 7/12.

questions.q: If x + 1/3 = 5/6, what is the value of x?
Find the rational number exactly midway between −7/9 and 4/15.
